items.title: Understanding and Improving Model Editing for Secure Code Generation
items.summary: This work systematically studies model editing as a model-level hardening mechanism for secure code generation, benchmarking three SOTA editors across multiple LLM families against CoSec on security, robustness, generalization, and functional correctness. Editing delivers larger security gains than CoSec on seen vulnerability types and is robust to prompt perturbations, but transfers unreliably to unseen vulnerabilities and can harm functional correctness. To address this, the authors introduce SafeEdit—functional tuning plus edit-aware regularization—which improves Pass@1 over UltraEdit across temperatures while largely preserving security, outperforms CoSec on security ratio, shows gains on CodeGuard+, and combines complementarily with CoSec.
items.why_it_matters: It offers an evidence-backed recipe (SafeEdit + optional CoSec) for hardening LLM code generators with better security–correctness trade-offs than inference-time only methods, informing defenses that don’t rely solely on runtime scaffolding.
items.reason: Calls out a critical evaluation flaw for generative time-series models on data with point masses; directly impacts benchmark validity and model comparisons for time-series foundation models.

items.title: A Six-Dimensional Taxonomy of Post-Training Adaptation Techniques with Applications in AI Governance
items.summary: This survey synthesizes post-training adaptation techniques—spanning retraining, fine-tuning, parameter-efficient adaptation, alignment, RAG, model editing, unlearning, calibration, and multimodal instruction tuning—and introduces a six-dimensional taxonomy by mechanism, goal, data requirement, persistence, structural scope, and model type. It clarifies conflated terms (e.g., fine-tuning vs. RAG vs. prompting), traces the evolution of adaptation across model eras, and maps relationships such as inheritance, supersession, hybridization, and layered deployment stacks. The work presents a vocabulary to support technical documentation, change tracking, and governance analysis, and highlights open challenges in evaluation, reproducibility, persistent inference-time adaptation, unlearning, multimodal adaptation, and governance-aware workflows.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a governance-aligned taxonomy that can standardize how LLM security adaptations (e.g., alignment, unlearning, RAG) are described, compared, and tracked across deployment stacks, aiding reproducible evaluation and auditability.
items.reason: Presents a timestep-conditioned transformer for global weather forecasting addressing timestep choice trade-offs—directly relevant to TSFM pretraining/objectives and long-horizon forecasting design.

items.title: Personalized Federated Sparse Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
items.summary: The paper proposes a personalized federated sparse adaptation framework for TSFMs in building energy forecasting, using a heterogeneous temporal MoE adapter placed after the pretrained representation and a sequence-level router that assigns each 168-hour window to top-k experts specialized for distinct temporal structures. It evaluates global FL, local training, and personalized FL variants with globally shared vs client-private expert banks across 50 buildings and three TSFM backbones. Results show personalization consistently outperforms Global FL-MoE and Local MoE, the best sparse-adaptation strategy depends on backbone and metric, and routing reveals client-level expert specialization, expert concentration, and near-uniform routing across backbones, implying adaptation should be client- and backbone-aware.
items.why_it_matters: Combines federated personalization with sparse MoE routing for TSFMs under non-IID meter data, offering actionable design signals (client-/backbone-aware adapters) relevant to secure on-device adaptation and privacy-preserving deployment.
items.reason: Federated personalization for TS foundation models directly matches the reader's primary interest in TSFMs and on-device/private data adaptation; MoE adapter and sparse adaptation are relevant to architecture and efficient adaptation.

items.title: Align-RAG: Alignment Is All You Need for TSFM In-Context Learning
items.summary: The paper introduces Align-RAG, a training-free method that applies closed-form amplitude rescaling and integer-lag phase alignment to retrieved past–future windows before feeding them to a frozen TSFM. On a frozen Chronos-Bolt, it outperforms a state-of-the-art trained retrieval adapter across seven benchmark datasets (average −3.75% MSE), and it also improves zero-shot MSE by 2.5%–13.7% on four additional frozen TSFMs without per-backbone tuning. Analysis shows aligned demonstrations induce prediction shifts in frozen backbones that track a closed-form ridge predictor on the same pairs, with a future-shuffle control ruling out futures-averaging, suggesting frozen TSFMs already support dynamic in-context use of retrievals.
items.why_it_matters: It challenges the need for learned fusion in RAG for forecasting by showing closed-form alignment on frozen backbones yields SOTA gains and ridge-like in-context adaptation, a strong baseline relevant to LLM alignment and retrieval studies.

items.title: The Horizon Gap: Planning, Memory, Execution, Training, and Evaluation for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.summary: The paper defines the horizon gap: LLMs that excel in single-pass reasoning still fail on multi-hour, multi-step tasks, and surveys 1,547 arXiv papers (2024–2026) collected via a systematic seed harvest with a 26.8% bleed filter plus targeted supplementation. It distinguishes long-horizon, long-context, and long-term memory, and organizes the literature into six lifecycle categories (planning, memory, execution, training, evaluation, foundations/safety) crossed with where horizons are carried (within-context, within-task-beyond-context, cross-task-persistent). A recurring finding is that outcome-only signals become uninformative as horizons increase, prompting methods that create denser step-level signals (e.g., process rewards, credit assignment, trajectory diagnostics), and the paper highlights open measurement problems around decomposing model vs. harness capability, correlated bias in process-level signals, and the possibility of a general predictive theory of long-horizon reliability.

items.title: Deployable Per-Instance Multi-Layer Activation Steering for Large Language Models
items.summary: The paper shows that in activation steering, the optimal injection layers vary per input, with per-instance multi-layer selection outperforming any fixed global layer set across six binary persona traits on two 8B models. A greedy layer-ranking rule based on single-layer marginal effects nearly matches a per-instance oracle but requires gold labels, so the authors train a prompt-only predictor to mimic it and propose a deployable recipe: a prompt-based per-instance layer ranker, a classifier to infer steering direction, and an adaptive gate that limits layers by short steered passes. This deployable approach recovers most of the oracle’s gains, avoids dropping below unsteered baselines on average, reduces fluency collapse relative to strong global selection, and is supported by a mechanistic account emphasizing direction over magnitude that explains misdirection flips, collapse from over-steering, and unsteerable ceilings.
items.why_it_matters: It operationalizes per-instance, label-free activation steering with adaptive multi-layer control, offering a practical path to safer, targeted behavior edits without sacrificing fluency—relevant to red-teaming defenses and controllable generation, and conceptually aligned with direction-based causal hypotheses familiar in interpretability.
items.reason: Per-instance multi-layer activation steering directly targets editing/model control at inference time—relevant to attack/defense surfaces, deployment, and efficient selective interventions for LLM security and agent behavior.

items.title: KReF: Training-Free Retrieval for Long-Term Time-Series Forecasting and Predictive Uncertainty
items.summary: KReF is a training-free retrieval framework for probabilistic long-term time-series forecasting that uses similar historical lookback–future pairs as a local empirical predictive distribution. It embeds lookbacks via handcrafted statistics or frozen random Fourier features, defines predictive masses and quantiles directly from similarity weights (also yielding CRPS and a weighted-mean point forecast), and adapts intervals using a probability-integral-transform map with validation-selected expansion/shrinkage. On six LTSF benchmarks across four horizons, KReF achieves the lowest CRPS in all 12 dataset–embedding settings and lowest IS90 in 9, with point forecasts matching or surpassing trained baselines on two datasets, and an archive-oracle analysis indicating further gains from finer routing.
items.why_it_matters: Introduces a strong training-free retrieval prior for LTSF with competitive uncertainty calibration, suggesting a complementary path to learned sequence models and a retrieval-centric lens relevant to LLM/security retrieval pipelines.
items.reason: Training-free retrieval for long-horizon probabilistic forecasting targets long-term TS forecasting and uncertainty without training—highly relevant to TSFM evaluation and lightweight inference approaches.

items.title: Telemetry and Concealment in Self-Adapting Generative AI: Logging Architecture, Adversarial Model Hiding, and the Limits of Detection
items.summary: The paper addresses governance for self-updating generative models by proposing a telemetry architecture that operates in discrete and continuous time, including a Minimal Sufficient Statistic for audits, a Merkle-chain for discrete weight sequences, an Ito-based continuous-time generalization, and KL divergence stopping-time logging. It then formalizes the Model Hiding Problem under adversarial providers and catalogs six attack strategies against the telemetry architecture across discrete and continuous time, providing a countermeasure for each. The result is a dual-regime approach where continuous telemetry narrows but cannot replace periodic invasive audits, aligning with traditional MRM pillars and remaining architecture-agnostic.
items.why_it_matters: It offers concrete telemetry and adversarial-resilience mechanisms directly applicable to secure deployment and monitoring of self-adapting LLMs and time-series models where online weight updates break standard validation.
items.reason: Directly addresses governance and detection challenges for self-adapting generative models, including telemetry and concealment—highly relevant to security, operational risk, and monitoring of adaptive LLMs.

items.title: Mind the Hook: Source-Level Auditing of Privacy Defenses in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: The paper argues that black-box privacy scores for RAG are hard to interpret without knowing which pipeline hook a defense actually activates, and proposes an active-path audit that inventories source-level hooks (retrieval, retrieved content, generation), maps metrics to leakage channels, and validates generated-text effects with exact-match canaries. In their benchmark reimplementations, DP-style defenses only modify retrieval scores while generation hooks are stubbed, explaining changes in membership inference but No-Defense-level performance on generated-text NEL_strict. In contrast, an end-to-end LPRAG path is canary-validated on the email channel, reducing recoveries from 53/150 (No-Defense) to 0/150, with the caveat that results reflect their reimplementations and stack, not a universal ranking.
items.why_it_matters: It offers a concrete auditing methodology to localize where RAG privacy defenses actually operate and which leakage channels their reported metrics truly measure—useful for designing, evaluating, and comparing LLM security defenses and metrics.

llm-security.title: DiffSafeMerge: Mitigating Backdoor Inheritance in Diffusion Model Merging

Evaluated across four attacks, two datasets, and 21 targets, DSM preserves zero worst-target ASR where intended merging already had it, eliminates remaining matches over three seeds even when baseline ASR was 48–100%, and among methods with zero worst-target ASR on both datasets achieves the lowest case-averaged FID in the seed-0 comparison.

llm-security.reason: Telemetry and concealment for self-adapting generative AI addresses governance and detection limits for models that modify themselves in production—important for model-risk management, attack concealment, and detection strategies.

llm-security.title: SkillsMetric: Mapping the Detection Boundary of Static Analysis for Malicious Agent Skills

llm-security.title: Skill-Use: Can LLMs Actually Use Skills in Agentic Harnesses?
llm-security.summary: The paper introduces Skill-Use, a benchmark that tests whether LLM agents can recognize, retrieve, and apply structured skills under progressive disclosure, separating Trigger, Compliance, and Boundary facets and combining them into an SU score that only credits execution after triggering. llm-security.title: When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents
llm-security.summary: The paper shows that self-evolving LLM agents experience a capability-contamination phase transition: beyond a critical pool size, newly distilled skills degrade performance due to defective skills seeding cross-round contamination chains. They demonstrate structural irreversibility, where post-hoc removal of source skills recovers only a small fraction of performance, motivating pre-commit gating via Verifier-as-Gatekeeper (VaG) with three heterogeneous critics and marginal-gain subset selection. On Terminal-Bench 2, unconditional accumulation peaks then degrades with limited rollback recovery, while VaG improves every round to 72% pass@1 with a ~5x smaller pool and transfers positively to other backbones and a second benchmark, with ablations showing the critics are complementary and non-substitutable.

llm-security.title: DBLAST: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding

llm-security.title: Evaluation Pitfalls and Sparsity Limitations in LLM-based Confidence Estimates for Classification
llm-security.summary: The paper finds that common LLM confidence verbalization for classification is extremely sparse, e.g., Qwen3-32B yields only eight unique values on SST-2 with over half at exactly 95%, a pattern repeated across four datasets and two LLMs. This sparsity skews evaluation: AUARC rankings change drastically depending on interpolation choice, with consistency sampling dropping from best to worst under stepwise vs. linear interpolation, motivating a call to standardize stepwise interpolation. llm-security.title: Align-RAG: Alignment Is All You Need for TSFM In-Context Learning

Analysis shows aligned demonstrations induce prediction shifts in frozen backbones that track a closed-form ridge predictor on the same pairs, with a future-shuffle control ruling out futures-averaging, suggesting frozen TSFMs already support dynamic in-context use of retrievals.

adversarial-ml.title: Gradient Immunity: Null-Space Resistance to Malicious Fine-Tuning
adversarial-ml.summary: The paper targets the PPOW setting where most weights are trainable but a small safety-critical component is preserved, and proposes a Unidirectional Safety Gate implemented as a Null Space Cubic Layer plus an Inverse Adapter after the final Transformer layer. adversarial-ml.summary: The paper introduces VectorHijack-SR, a black-box measurement method that turns paired victim/base residuals into calibrated bounds over PEFT family, layer locality, and coarse rank, using aggregated query-level statistics and a service-disjoint classifier plus a cross-fitted hierarchical rejector to test LoRA-manifold membership. Despite measurable structural leakage, experiments show a visibility–exploitability gap: two-stage recovery offers no fair-budget query savings, posterior-selected PEFT underperforms distill-then-convert PEFT, and free-running generation remains near chance.

adversarial-ml.title: The Label Defines the Timescale: Trait-State Limits of Temporal-Aggregate Learning
adversarial-ml.summary: The paper analyzes labels of temporal aggregates Θ_{g,T} built from a latent Gaussian process with a stable trait and correlated state, using an exact protocol-conditioned Bayes-risk identity. It shows label variance splits into an O(1) trait and O(T^{-1}) state component, derives task-dependent effective temporal spans (means tied to ordinary correlation time; occupation times to higher-order spectra), and proves state-driven occupation-label variance peaks at trait-threshold with window efficiency decaying slowly away from it. With a fixed segment budget, risks and simulations show repeated co-temporal segments saturate quickly while temporally dispersed observations keep improving state explainability; trait ceilings come from test-retest quantities, whereas state ceilings need short-lag calibration, implying observed limits can be protocol-driven rather than architectural.
adversarial-ml.why_it_matters: Clarifies when snapshot protocols fundamentally cap aggregate-label predictability and how to design observation schedules to separate architectural limits from acquisition ceilings—directly relevant to security evals of LLM temporal tasks and to designing time series foundation model benchmarks.

tsfm.title: KReF: Training-Free Retrieval for Long-Term Time-Series Forecasting and Predictive Uncertainty

tsfm.reason: Elastic retrievers/rerankers address scalable retrieval tradeoffs and dynamic model-size/runtime adaptation—useful for efficient RAG/agent pipelines and evaluation of retrieval components in security workflows.

tsfm.title: Model Discovery Agent: LLM-assisted Bayesian experiment design for data-efficient discovery of mechanistic world models
tsfm.reason: LLM-assisted Bayesian experiment design for data-efficient discovery of mechanistic models speaks to sample-efficient model identification and coupling LLM proposers with SMC — relevant for time-series/physical-model discovery and efficient experimentation.

tsfm.title: Causal State-Space Model for Causal Inference: Estimating Longitudinal Individual Treatment Effects
tsfm.reason: Presents a causal state-space model for longitudinal ITE estimation addressing representation-treatment confounds—useful for causal/time-series modeling and evaluation of counterfactual prediction under domain shifts.

tsfm.title: TS-RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation for Time Series Forecasting
tsfm.summary: The paper proposes TS-RAG, a retrieval-augmented approach for time series forecasting that uses specially designed reference tokens to fuse input sequences with retrieved similar sequences. It argues that naive concatenation of references, as in LLM RAG, is ineffective for typical time series models due to limited data, smaller scales, and weaker generative ability. Experiments show TS-RAG achieves consistent state-of-the-art results on several real-world forecasting benchmarks.
tsfm.why_it_matters: It bridges LLM-style RAG with time series by introducing a tailored fusion mechanism, offering a concrete path to leverage retrieval for stronger temporal forecasting without requiring LLM-scale models.
tsfm.reason: Tabular foundation model adaptation via gated skill evolution is relevant for transfer and training-free adaptation methods, but focused on tabular rather than temporal sequence models.

tsfm.title: SkillTFM: Gated Skill Evolution for Training-Free Adaptation of Tabular Foundation Models
tsfm.summary: The paper introduces SkillTFM, a training-free adaptation system for tabular foundation models that replaces parameter updates with gated evolution of agentic skills. It uses a verifiable, extensible skill bank combining boundary evidence identification to characterize task structure and base-model failures with gated skill evolution to retrieve and extend reusable skills under explicit validation. In simulated boundary settings and real-world electricity-price forecasting, SkillTFM improves AUC by 0.128–0.142, elevating nonlinear-boundary AUC from 0.699 to 0.898, and shows effectiveness across different TFM backbones.
tsfm.why_it_matters: It proposes a security-adjacent, verifiable skill-gating mechanism for training-free adaptation under distribution shift, echoing modular skill libraries and guarded tool-use in LLMs while targeting tabular/time-series TFMs.
tsfm.reason: Empirical study of self-pretraining for medical time series—useful data on pretraining benefits and transfer in noisy, multimodal TS settings though domain-specific.

tsfm.title: Taxonomy-Driven Analysis of Open-Source AI Risk Mitigation Tools
tsfm.reason: Using VLMs to encode time-series as images speaks to practical efficiency and cross-modal approaches for time-series analysis and could impact deployment/serving costs for TS workloads.

tsfm.title: Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension
tsfm.reason: Analysis of continual pretraining via spectral methods and head importance could inform efficient adaptation and pruning for domain-specialized LLMs; some mechanistic insights may transfer to TSFM architectures.

agents.title: HarnessSafe: Evaluating Safety Across Persistent Carriers in Agent Harnesses
agents.summary: The paper introduces HarnessSafe, a benchmark of 328 executable cases spanning seven persistent-carrier families to assess delayed safety risks in agent harnesses that persist state across tasks and sessions. Each case is defined as a Persistent-Risk Lifecycle that traces attacker influence from entry through cross-carrier persistence to a benign trigger and an observable violation, and a multi-stage, trace-based evaluation measures how far each attack progresses and where it is stopped. Experiments indicate containment is carrier-specific and depends strongly on the harness-model configuration, with both harness and model shaping outcomes and attack success rates failing to capture lifecycle progression patterns.
agents.why_it_matters: It offers a carrier-aware, trace-based methodology and dataset to dissect how safety risks propagate across memory/tools/skills in agentic systems—complementing coarse success-rate metrics and informing defense design in LLM agents and persistent pipelines.
agents.reason: Benchmarks delayed safety risks from persistent carriers in agent harnesses; directly targets attack surfaces (memory, tools, skills), evaluation methodology, and end-to-end exploit propagation — highly relevant to LLM security and agentic threat models.

agents.title: Toward Metacognitive One-Shot Indirect Prompt Injection: Strategy Abstraction Via Outcome-Conditioned Reflection
agents.summary: The paper introduces SAVOR, a one-shot IPI attack framework that moves adaptation offline via outcome-conditioned reflection over successful and failed trajectories from disjoint training environments, consolidating validated, context-conditioned strategies into a reusable strategy memory. At test time, the frozen memory generates a single payload per unseen target without iterative interaction or feedback, achieving the highest average attack success rate across two benchmarks and three victim models. On Agent Security Bench and the new executable OpenClaw-IPI, SAVOR outperforms the strongest prior attack by 2.5–11.8 points and beats the same injection channel without strategy learning by 23.1 and 28.6 points respectively, with learned memory transferring across defenses.
agents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates practical one-shot IPI via offline strategy distillation that generalizes across tools, goals, and defenses—relevant for red-teaming LLM agents and for designing defenses that hold under realistic single-interaction constraints.
agents.reason: One-shot indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks on tool-using agents via offline strategy distillation directly targets agentic attack surfaces and realistic attacker models—highly relevant to LLM security and red-teaming methodology.

agents.title: ColluSkill: Adversarial Cross-Skill Composition for Evading Agent Skill Scanners
agents.summary: The paper identifies a blind spot in LLM agent security: existing scanners mostly vet individual skills, missing harms that emerge from cross-skill composition. It introduces ColluSkill, a collusive multi-skill-chain attack that splits malicious intent into interdependent, locally plausible sub-skills and uses LLM-based chain planning plus scanner-feedback refinement to evade detection. To defend, the authors propose ChainGuard, a context-aware skill-chain scanner that reconstructs cross-skill dependencies and artifact flows, showing ColluSkill attains 96.0% ASR against six scanners, which ChainGuard reduces to 22.5% while keeping 99.5% benign workflows.
agents.why_it_matters: Highlights a concrete, high-success collusive attack and a chain-level defense paradigm directly relevant to secure LLM-agent composition and scanning beyond single-skill analysis.
agents.reason: Cross-skill collusion exposing blind spots in skill scanners attacks agent skill composition and practical defense gaps—high priority for agent security, scanner evaluation, and red-team design.

agents.title: From Runnable to Verifiable: An Independent Reproducibility Study of LLM/Agent-Driven Vulnerability Validation Artifacts
agents.summary: This pre-registered reproducibility audit examines LLM/agent-driven vulnerability validation artifacts across 104 papers (2023–2026), finding only 59 with publicly reachable artifacts and executing 18 paper-level workflows and 102 anchor benchmark cases. It reports high mismatch and fragility: 58/102 anchor cases have internal CVE IDs diverging from directory labels; only 10/18 artifacts run end-to-end at R0 (11/18 after R1 env-only fixes); and embedded oracles are unreliable, with 20/30 patched-counterfactuals still signaling and 7/19 negative controls triggering, yielding oracle sensitivity 60% and specificity 45%. The study argues that vulnerable-build triggers are not CVE-specific evidence without a clean patched counterfactual and offers a reusable, pre-registered protocol (post-conditions, R0/R1 repair ladder, G1–G3 evidence levels, patched-counterfactual oracles) for the community.
agents.why_it_matters: It surfaces concrete failure modes and a reusable protocol for verifying LLM/agent security claims—directly informing eval design, oracle construction, and counterfactual controls for both LLM security and time-series-style benchmark reproducibility.
agents.reason: ActBench proposes an execution-trajectory-based behavioral safety benchmark for cowork agents, directly applicable to evaluating agent risks like data leakage and unauthorized actions—highly relevant for tooling and red-teaming.

agents.title: ElasticBack: Stealthy Conditional Backdoor in LLM-Agent Skills via Coupled Trigger-Rule Optimization
agents.summary: The paper introduces ElasticBack, a conditional single-skill backdoor for LLM agents that couples a malicious rule R in the skill document with a benign-looking trigger T in user queries, activating only when both appear. It constructs R via semantic-anchored rule injection and then fixes R while evolving T using a stealth-constrained genetic search to optimize attack effectiveness and stealth without modifying model weights. Experiments over three target behaviors (50 skills each) and four agent LLMs show high ASR with near-zero FPR, preserved clean accuracy, cross-model transfer, and evasion of deployment-time defenses, motivating stronger supply-chain defenses for skills.
agents.why_it_matters: Highlights a practical, weight-free, conditional backdoor vector in the emerging agent skill ecosystem, relevant to securing tool-using LLMs and evaluating defenses against stealthy trigger-rule couplings.
agents.reason: Presents a stealthy conditional backdoor attack targeting agent skills (supply-chain threat) with low-cost single-skill triggers—highly relevant to LLM agent security, tool/skill poisoning, and defense evaluation.

agents.title: When Experience Becomes Instruction: Trajectory Poisoning in Self-Evolving Agent Skill Systems
agents.summary: The paper introduces PoisonedEvolution, a trajectory-poisoning attack on self-evolving skill (SES) systems that distill agent trajectories into persistent skills, where an attacker with skill-level black-box access contributes bounded evidence to influence skill promotion. It formalizes artifact poisoning as requiring Inclusion, Evolution Attribution, and Realization, identifying Attribution—making target behaviors appear causally useful, recurrent, and generalizable—as the key bottleneck, and demonstrates high success embedding target behaviors across six LLM evolvers in SkillClaw (91.0% SER) and transfer to Trace2Skill (61.5% SER) at 10% attacker support. Controlled studies show three consistent attacker records in a 30-record batch suffice while one is much weaker, and ablations highlight recurring support, causal framing, and domain-aligned encoding as main success factors, framing evidence promotion as a critical security boundary for self-evolving agents.
agents.why_it_matters: It pinpoints the promotion/attribution step in skill evolution as an attack surface with quantified vulnerability and transferable effects, informing defenses for agentic LLMs and data-driven skill distillation pipelines.
agents.reason: Robust context-aware segmentation for malicious instructions (IPI) targets detection of embedded prompt injections tailored to a query—highly relevant to defending agents and evaluating instruction-level attacks.

agents.title: Towards a Risk Assessment of Malicious Skill Files in Coding Agents
agents.summary: The paper studies the attack surface introduced by agent skill folders in autonomous coding agents and presents an adversarial skill-synthesis method that converts 471 real shell commands into 2,826 benign-looking skills mapped to 11 ATT&CK tactics using six LLMs. It introduces a reproducible evaluation pipeline with stratification, evidence anchoring, refusal veto, and a deterministic declared-intent override, using a three-judge LLM panel validated against a blind human gold standard (κ=0.85). In large-scale tests (5,629 runs), Gemini CLI was exploited in 95.5–96.1% and Qwen Code in 71.6–74.0% of runs with only 1.99% explicit safety recognition, and code/dataset are released at https://github.com/awsm-research/AgentJailbreak.
agents.why_it_matters: Provides a validated benchmark, eval pipeline, and high-base-rate exploitation evidence for skill-file attacks in coding agents—directly relevant to LLM security evals and agentic deployment risk.
agents.reason: Demonstrates pipeline attack surface in coding agents by hiding malicious shell commands in natural-language skill files — directly applicable to agentic-system attack vectors and red-teaming.

agents.title: Deployable Per-Instance Multi-Layer Activation Steering for Large Language Models
agents.summary: The paper shows that in activation steering, the optimal injection layers vary per input, with per-instance multi-layer selection outperforming any fixed global layer set across six binary persona traits on two 8B models. A greedy layer-ranking rule based on single-layer marginal effects nearly matches a per-instance oracle but requires gold labels, so the authors train a prompt-only predictor to mimic it and propose a deployable recipe: a prompt-based per-instance layer ranker, a classifier to infer steering direction, and an adaptive gate that limits layers by short steered passes. This deployable approach recovers most of the oracle’s gains, avoids dropping below unsteered baselines on average, reduces fluency collapse relative to strong global selection, and is supported by a mechanistic account emphasizing direction over magnitude that explains misdirection flips, collapse from over-steering, and unsteerable ceilings.
agents.why_it_matters: It operationalizes per-instance, label-free activation steering with adaptive multi-layer control, offering a practical path to safer, targeted behavior edits without sacrificing fluency—relevant to red-teaming defenses and controllable generation, and conceptually aligned with direction-based causal hypotheses familiar in interpretability.
agents.reason: Per-instance multi-layer activation steering directly targets editing/model control at inference time—relevant to attack/defense surfaces, deployment, and efficient selective interventions for LLM security and agent behavior.

agents.title: Activation Probes Surface Code-Security Signals that the Model's Output Misses
agents.summary: The authors study whether linear probes on open-weight reviewer models’ activations reveal code-security signals that the same models’ outputs miss. Trained on paired vulnerable/fixed Python functions and evaluated zero-shot on real disclosed vulns (including unseen weakness types) across five models, a single probe per model ranks the vulnerable version above its fix in 61–67% of single-function-fix cases, exceeding chance and the model’s own prompted YES/NO logit-based decisions under all prompts tested. Written verdicts (including CoT) typically fail to distinguish vulnerable from fixed code, suggesting activations encode a security signal not surfaced by prompting.
agents.why_it_matters: It shows latent security-relevant information in LLM activations can be extracted with simple probes even when model outputs fail, informing red-teaming, interpretability, and toolstack design for secure code generation with closed-weight agents + open-weight reviewers.
agents.reason: Probing activations to surface vulnerabilities that outputs miss offers an interpretable detection avenue for code-security in generated artifacts—valuable for scalable review and red-team tooling.

agents.title: SkillsMetric: Mapping the Detection Boundary of Static Analysis for Malicious Agent Skills
agents.summary: This work introduces SkillsMetric, a five-stage static analysis framework that scores LLM agent skills across pattern density, statistical anomaly, dataflow taint, import anomaly, and capability mismatch. Using an adversarial dataset of 2,266 skills covering 16 attack types and the SkillMD-138K corpus, it reports AUC 0.93 and 5-fold CV F1 73.4%±0.5%, with 93% detection for data exfiltration and steganographic payloads. It also exposes blind spots—0% detection for host destruction via common shell commands and 42% for prompt injection—arguing static analysis alone is insufficient and should be paired with semantic review in defense-in-depth.
agents.why_it_matters: Directly maps the detection boundary of static analysis for agent skills, highlighting failure modes (e.g., prompt injection, host destruction) that inform red-teaming, hybrid detection pipelines, and security benchmarks for LLM agents.
agents.reason: Static analysis scoring of agent 'skills' maps to supply-chain and capability-based attack surfaces for LLM agents and helps red-teaming/defense of tool-augmented systems.

agents.title: Persistent Semantic Entities in Tool-Augmented LLM Systems
agents.reason: Inference-time guard that routes capabilities to avoid reasoning-centric jailbreaks targets a new, practical jailbreak class and proposes model-agnostic mitigations relevant for deployment.

agents.title: Rethinking Self-Evolving Agents: Do We Still Need Prescribed Optimization Pipelines?
agents.reason: Examines self-evolving agents and whether prescribed optimization pipelines remain necessary when using frontier models as optimizers—important for agent safety, emergent optimization behaviors, and red-teaming agentic pipelines.

agents.title: Skill-Use: Can LLMs Actually Use Skills in Agentic Harnesses?
agents.summary: The paper introduces Skill-Use, a benchmark that tests whether LLM agents can recognize, retrieve, and apply structured skills under progressive disclosure, separating Trigger, Compliance, and Boundary facets and combining them into an SU score that only credits execution after triggering. It comprises 79 real skills and 177 executable tasks across nine domains, run in Docker sandboxes and scored via trajectory-based rubrics, and evaluates eight LLMs across two agent harnesses. Results show reliable skill use is not yet achieved (best SU 0.613), with triggering and procedural compliance as independent bottlenecks and scores/model rankings varying by harness, indicating skill use is harness-conditioned rather than an inherent model property.
agents.why_it_matters: It provides a rigorous, execution-grounded way to diagnose harness-conditioned failure modes (triggering vs. compliance vs. boundary) in tool-using LLM agents, informing both security-sensitive agent design and modular capability evaluation akin to time-series foundation model benchmarking.
agents.reason: Skill-Use evaluates whether agents can recognize and retrieve procedural skills under partial disclosure—directly relevant to agentic systems, tool-use security surfaces and evaluation methodology for skill-based attacks/robustness.

agents.title: verdi: retrieval is not transfer for continual world model optimization
agents.reason: Argues that retrieved strategies don't directly transfer for optimizing world models and proposes safeguarding transfer—relevant to continual optimization of foundation world/time-series models and efficient automated optimization agents.

agents.title: RouteGuard: Certifying Routing Gain in LLM Multi-Agent Systems When Complementarity Is Not Enough
agents.reason: Analyzes routing certification in LLM multi-advisor systems and provides finite-sample guarantees for when routing yields deployable gain—relevant to safe agent composition, evaluation metrics beyond AUC, and deployment-risk assessment.

agents.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
agents.summary: The paper introduces HarnessOpt-Bench, a benchmark for end-to-end harness optimization where an LLM optimizer iteratively edits a target agent’s harness under expensive, stochastic evaluation with a fixed budget, using only graded feedback and without access to a held-out test partition. A trusted execution environment enforces evaluation boundaries, meters resource use, and preserves candidate versions for audit, and performance is measured by normalized gain over the seed harness. Evaluating five frontier LLMs across four tasks and 111 runs, the authors find optimizer models differentiate more than coding harnesses, native harnesses aren’t consistently superior, and gains vary substantially by task and seed regime, establishing harness optimization as a measurable and discriminative capability with room for improvement.
agents.why_it_matters: It provides a rigorous, auditable setup to compare LLMs’ agentic self-improvement under realistic noisy/expensive evals—relevant for secure agent orchestration and optimizing time-series/tool-using pipelines.
agents.reason: Benchmark for optimizing agent harnesses is directly relevant to LLM agent security (attack surface via prompts/tools/orchestration) and offers an evaluation protocol useful for red-teaming and robust harness design.

agents.title: When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents
agents.summary: The paper shows that self-evolving LLM agents experience a capability-contamination phase transition: beyond a critical pool size, newly distilled skills degrade performance due to defective skills seeding cross-round contamination chains. They demonstrate structural irreversibility, where post-hoc removal of source skills recovers only a small fraction of performance, motivating pre-commit gating via Verifier-as-Gatekeeper (VaG) with three heterogeneous critics and marginal-gain subset selection. On Terminal-Bench 2, unconditional accumulation peaks then degrades with limited rollback recovery, while VaG improves every round to 72% pass@1 with a ~5x smaller pool and transfers positively to other backbones and a second benchmark, with ablations showing the critics are complementary and non-substitutable.
agents.why_it_matters: It surfaces an irreversible contamination mechanism in skill distillation and proposes a concrete pre-commit gating framework that stabilizes agent evolution and transfers across models/benchmarks, directly relevant to secure, scalable LLM agent training and model-based control of evolving skill libraries.
agents.reason: Findings about self-evolving agent skill contamination directly impact safety of agent self-improvement and distillation pipelines—important for red-teaming and mitigation strategies.

agents.title: DBLAST: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding
agents.summary: The paper analyzes speculative decoding with block/diffusion drafters and shows that assuming conditional independence across drafted positions breaks down under non-greedy, higher-entropy target sampling, reducing accepted draft length. It introduces DBLAST, a dependent block drafter using a low-rank latent mixture over token positions plus an acceptance-oriented objective that optimizes expected verified length. Experiments on Qwen3-4B/8B across GSM8K, MT-Bench, HumanEval, and creative-writing benchmarks report consistent gains in accepted length over independent block sampling, particularly at higher entropy.
agents.why_it_matters: It targets stochastic decoding efficiency—key for secure, diverse sampling and alignment workflows—by improving acceptance rates under high-entropy regimes, informing both LLM safety pipelines and efficient inference design.
agents.reason: Speculative decoding for stochastic drafts impacts efficient inference for agents and could change threat surface of model outputs when combined with stochasticity — relevant to scalable red-teaming and secure deployment.

agents.title: EdgeXpert: An Edge Device for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference with Mixture-of-Experts and Speculative Decoding
agents.summary: EdgeXpert is a software-hardware co-designed LLM accelerator targeting the EMA bottleneck in FFN layers for on-device inference, combining speculative decoding with MoE despite their typical incompatibility. In prefill, it uses prompt-wise expert reuse by selecting important tokens via a lightweight encoder to build a shared expert set and routes less important tokens with a reduced expert budget to cut expert EMA; in decode, depth-aware expert coalescing loads only salient channels across same-depth speculative candidates and applies computational calibration to maintain accuracy without extra memory access. Implemented in Samsung 28nm at 800 MHz, EdgeXpert reports up to 56.3% latency and 44.1% energy reductions versus prior work while maintaining near-baseline accuracy.
agents.why_it_matters: It offers a practical path to marry MoE with speculative decoding for memory-bound edge inference, yielding sizable latency/energy gains relevant to secure, private on-device LLM deployment and efficient time-sensitive workloads.
agents.reason: Skill Entropy offers a quantitative measure and training signal for cross-skill long-horizon reasoning, useful for designing and evaluating agents and long-horizon benchmarks relevant to TSFM-style sequence tasks.

agents.title: Trident : How to Break Deep Reinforcement Learning Cyber Defenses (Agentic)
agents.summary: The paper introduces Trident, an agentic LLM red-teaming framework for evaluating DRL-based cyber defenses, consisting of a dynamic benchmark across CybORG CAGE 4 and CyberWheel, a dataset of 13k+ red-blue trajectories for RLVR, and a Code-as-Policy RLVR architecture. Trident reframes red-agent training as a contextual bandit using a Log Summarizer–Planner–Coder pipeline, where a trainable Planner produces complete attack strategies from compressed logs and a frozen Coder turns them into executable Python policies against live DRL defenders. Empirically, a single 7B planner substantially degrades blue-agent performance (average 522% reduction vs. static red baselines) and uncovers emergent behaviors like decoy avoidance and adaptive state prioritization that static heuristics miss.
agents.why_it_matters: It demonstrates an RLVR-driven, code-generating agent that reliably breaks DRL cyber defenses and provides a benchmark/dataset, directly informing LLM security evaluation and agent robustness research.
agents.reason: Provides trajectory-level certification methods for modular LLM-based security agents, addressing guarantees and calibration across multi-stage pipelines — useful for safety evaluation of agentic security systems.

agents.title: Align-RAG: Alignment Is All You Need for TSFM In-Context Learning
agents.summary: The paper introduces Align-RAG, a training-free method that applies closed-form amplitude rescaling and integer-lag phase alignment to retrieved past–future windows before feeding them to a frozen TSFM. On a frozen Chronos-Bolt, it outperforms a state-of-the-art trained retrieval adapter across seven benchmark datasets (average −3.75% MSE), and it also improves zero-shot MSE by 2.5%–13.7% on four additional frozen TSFMs without per-backbone tuning. Analysis shows aligned demonstrations induce prediction shifts in frozen backbones that track a closed-form ridge predictor on the same pairs, with a future-shuffle control ruling out futures-averaging, suggesting frozen TSFMs already support dynamic in-context use of retrievals.
agents.why_it_matters: It challenges the need for learned fusion in RAG for forecasting by showing closed-form alignment on frozen backbones yields SOTA gains and ridge-like in-context adaptation, a strong baseline relevant to LLM alignment and retrieval studies.
agents.reason: DASH improves on-policy self-distillation for reasoning models with temporally-adaptive supervision horizons — relevant to improving RL-style fine-tuning and evaluation of reasoning/judging behavior and scalable red-teaming.

agents.title: FutureBridge: Token Selection Beyond Local Preference in Collaborative Decoding
agents.summary: FutureBridge proposes a token reranking scheme for LLM–SLM collaborative decoding that prioritizes tokens enabling the SLM’s subsequent reasoning rather than the LLM’s local preference. Training uses an answer-verified LLM trajectory to fix a shared future, while a frozen SLM assigns counterfactual scores to candidate tokens under this common context to supervise a lightweight reranker observing only the current state and token. At inference, the LLM only expands the candidate pool and the reranker selects a single token before handing generation back to the SLM without appending any future suffix, yielding a 35.1% relative Math Avg. improvement for Qwen3-1.7B across five math reasoning benchmarks over greedy decoding.
agents.why_it_matters: It reframes collaboration as SLM-aware token selection, offering a practical path to safer, stronger small-model reasoning with minimal LLM involvement—relevant to alignment, tool-use gating, and cost/security tradeoffs in cooperative decoding.
agents.reason: FutureBridge proposes collaborative decoding between LLM and smaller models to improve SLM reasoning—relevant for efficient red-teaming, agent pipelines, and attack/defense strategies where token choice affects downstream agent behavior.

agents.title: EMAS: Stabilizing Multi-Agent System Evolution through Evidence-Guided Revision
agents.reason: Improves automated multi-agent system revision without parameter updates—useful for agent robustness, low-cost red-teaming, and deployment evolution.

agents.title: MemWM: Memory-Augmented Text-Based World Model
agents.summary: MemWM is a memory-augmented text world model that conditions next-state imagination on a curated memory bank of transition rules, state caches, and hard-to-predict facts. It introduces Structured State Fidelity (SSF) to evaluate factual state preservation and shows that memory-augmented training improves SSF by up to 206.3% over SFT. In planning, they freeze the policy and supply policy-side world skill via retrieved task-level skills and step-wise corrective guidance, yielding up to a 65.4% relative success gain across ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld, with sensitivity analyses showing benefits across memory and action budgets.
agents.why_it_matters: Targets a key failure mode in text-based world models—systematic state-transition errors—using retrieval-style memory that cleanly composes with frozen policies, relevant to secure planning and robust long-horizon reasoning.
agents.reason: Memory-augmented world model aims to preserve factual state across imagined transitions — important for agent reliability and potential attack surfaces (memory corruption), though not explicitly about security.

agents.title: Beyond Solvability: Task Learnability as a Static Prior for LLM RL Post-Training
agents.reason: Proposes task learnability as a static prior to improve RL post-training sampling—relevant to efficient RLHF/RL fine-tuning and evaluation of curricula for eliciting reasoning in LLMs (methodology applicable to red-teaming and costly post-training regimes).

agents.reason: LLM-assisted Bayesian experiment design for data-efficient discovery of mechanistic models speaks to sample-efficient model identification and coupling LLM proposers with SMC — relevant for time-series/physical-model discovery and efficient experimentation.

agents.title: DreamGuard: Efficient Runtime Guardrail for LLM Agents via Risk-Aware World Model
agents.summary: DreamGuard is a proactive runtime guardrail for LLM agents that uses a risk-aware world model to track a compact recurrent latent state over trajectories and forecast future latent states. From these forecasts, it derives immediate-hazard and prefix-risk evidence and fuses multi-horizon signals to decide on interventions before tool executions. Across four benchmarks and an online evaluation, DreamGuard outperforms generic, reactive, and proactive baselines with the best safety-utility trade-off and averages 25 ms end-to-end latency per call.
agents.why_it_matters: Introduces a trajectory-aware, low-latency guardrail with explicit risk modeling, aligning with interests in long-horizon safety for LLM agents and bridging to sequence modeling ideas from time series foundation models.
agents.reason: Adaptive allocation across model populations for LLM-driven evolutionary search is relevant for cost-efficient red-teaming/evolutionary program search, but more about budgeting than core security.

agents.title: Runtime Observability for Heterogeneous Attention Memory
agents.summary: The paper proposes a runtime observability contract for heterogeneous attention memory that covers four memory classes with three operators, enforces metric-typed composition, and yields an executable request-level risk ledger whose certification tier (formal, partial, empirical) is machine-determined. They instantiate this across six model configurations over five architecture families, validate under 12.4M entry reads with eight-way concurrency and per-request budgets, and maintain zero risk-budget violations while using an always-on fused probe within CUDA graphs. Applied to a served DeepSeek-V4 stack with a packed compressed-KV prototype, the system localizes a silent corruption to a structural boundary and conducts a machine-adjudicated discrimination campaign that rejects two confounded inferences, with all artifacts and Lean proofs released for full regeneration.
agents.why_it_matters: It offers a principled, composable, and empirically backed way to quantify and bound memory-related risks in modern LLM serving stacks, directly relevant to secure KV/latent cache compression and recurrent state management in time-series-like attention regimes.
agents.reason: Addresses memory/cache observability and runtime contracts across attention/memory mechanisms — relevant for understanding failure modes under compression and for risk accounting in deployed LLMs and agents.

agents.title: Learning the Pareto Frontier of Predictive Models under Distribution Shift
agents.summary: The paper introduces Frontier Learning, which treats a library of pretrained models with mixed access regimes (black-box predictions and white-box representations) as complementary sources under distribution shift. It builds a unified target-domain feature by concatenating internal representations from white-box models with outputs from black-box models, then trains a lightweight regularized supervised learner, guaranteeing training-sample risk no worse than any single baseline including zero-shot reuse, fine-tuning, or direct training. Experiments on simulations and real-world shifts (DomainNet/VisDA and MIMIC-IV-Notes ICU mortality) show it matches or outperforms the strongest individual reuse strategy, with the largest gains when no single baseline is reliable across the shifts considered.
agents.why_it_matters: Provides a simple, access-agnostic ensemble-on-representations approach that subsumes common reuse strategies and is empirically strong under shift—relevant to robustness/security and modular reuse of foundation models.
agents.reason: Agentic BO using LLMs to inject priors into optimization touches on agentic systems and leveraging LLMs as components—relevant to attack/defense surfaces and efficient automated red-teaming workflows.

agents.reason: SpecRoll focuses on speculative decoding within RL rollouts to speed generation—relevant for efficient agentic RLHF/rollouts but not directly on LLM security or time-series foundations.

agents.reason: Practical pipeline for converting policies to machine-checkable constraints via agentic LLMs; useful for compliance automation but peripheral to core LLM security or TSFM research.

agents.reason: Practical pipeline for translating policies into formal constraints using LLMs and validators touches agentic system tooling and automated compliance verification, useful for governance/evaluation of agent behavior.

efficiency.reason: Model editing for secure code generation evaluates model-level hardening methods versus inference-time approaches — relevant to reducing malicious or vulnerable generations in deployed LLMs.

efficiency.reason: Argues that retrieved strategies don't directly transfer for optimizing world models and proposes safeguarding transfer—relevant to continual optimization of foundation world/time-series models and efficient automated optimization agents.

efficiency.title: DBLAST: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding
efficiency.summary: The paper analyzes speculative decoding with block/diffusion drafters and shows that assuming conditional independence across drafted positions breaks down under non-greedy, higher-entropy target sampling, reducing accepted draft length. It introduces DBLAST, a dependent block drafter using a low-rank latent mixture over token positions plus an acceptance-oriented objective that optimizes expected verified length. Experiments on Qwen3-4B/8B across GSM8K, MT-Bench, HumanEval, and creative-writing benchmarks report consistent gains in accepted length over independent block sampling, particularly at higher entropy.
efficiency.why_it_matters: It targets stochastic decoding efficiency—key for secure, diverse sampling and alignment workflows—by improving acceptance rates under high-entropy regimes, informing both LLM safety pipelines and efficient inference design.
efficiency.reason: Speculative decoding for stochastic drafts impacts efficient inference for agents and could change threat surface of model outputs when combined with stochasticity — relevant to scalable red-teaming and secure deployment.

efficiency.title: FutureBridge: Token Selection Beyond Local Preference in Collaborative Decoding
efficiency.summary: FutureBridge proposes a token reranking scheme for LLM–SLM collaborative decoding that prioritizes tokens enabling the SLM’s subsequent reasoning rather than the LLM’s local preference. Training uses an answer-verified LLM trajectory to fix a shared future, while a frozen SLM assigns counterfactual scores to candidate tokens under this common context to supervise a lightweight reranker observing only the current state and token. At inference, the LLM only expands the candidate pool and the reranker selects a single token before handing generation back to the SLM without appending any future suffix, yielding a 35.1% relative Math Avg. improvement for Qwen3-1.7B across five math reasoning benchmarks over greedy decoding.
efficiency.why_it_matters: It reframes collaboration as SLM-aware token selection, offering a practical path to safer, stronger small-model reasoning with minimal LLM involvement—relevant to alignment, tool-use gating, and cost/security tradeoffs in cooperative decoding.
efficiency.reason: FutureBridge proposes collaborative decoding between LLM and smaller models to improve SLM reasoning—relevant for efficient red-teaming, agent pipelines, and attack/defense strategies where token choice affects downstream agent behavior.

efficiency.title: Beyond Foundation Models: Dimension-Aware Neural Architecture Search with Small-Data Representation Models for Cryocooler Lifetime Prediction
efficiency.summary: The paper proposes FSD-RM, a paradigm of capacity-controlled, unsupervised representation models (CNN1D, LSTM, GRU, Transformer) for small, domain-specific time-series data, avoiding large-scale pretraining. It integrates these encoders into a two-stage pipeline for cryocooler lifetime prediction and uses dimension-aware NAS to jointly optimize model capacity and input dimensionality. Experiments on cryocooler telemetry show competitive predictive performance with reduced training cost and model complexity, enabled by explicit inductive bias and capacity control choices.
efficiency.why_it_matters: It presents a NAS-driven, small-data alternative to time-series FMs that could inform secure, resource-efficient modeling pipelines when pretraining data are scarce or restricted.
efficiency.reason: Proposes small-data representation models for time-series forecasting in domain-limited settings—directly relevant to time-series foundation-model alternatives and practical architectures.

efficiency.title: Tevatron-Elastic: A Unified Abstraction for Training Elastic Retrievers and Rerankers
efficiency.reason: Elastic retrievers/rerankers address scalable retrieval tradeoffs and dynamic model-size/runtime adaptation—useful for efficient RAG/agent pipelines and evaluation of retrieval components in security workflows.

efficiency.title: Model Discovery Agent: LLM-assisted Bayesian experiment design for data-efficient discovery of mechanistic world models
efficiency.reason: LLM-assisted Bayesian experiment design for data-efficient discovery of mechanistic models speaks to sample-efficient model identification and coupling LLM proposers with SMC — relevant for time-series/physical-model discovery and efficient experimentation.

efficiency.title: DreamGuard: Efficient Runtime Guardrail for LLM Agents via Risk-Aware World Model
efficiency.summary: DreamGuard is a proactive runtime guardrail for LLM agents that uses a risk-aware world model to track a compact recurrent latent state over trajectories and forecast future latent states. From these forecasts, it derives immediate-hazard and prefix-risk evidence and fuses multi-horizon signals to decide on interventions before tool executions. Across four benchmarks and an online evaluation, DreamGuard outperforms generic, reactive, and proactive baselines with the best safety-utility trade-off and averages 25 ms end-to-end latency per call.
efficiency.why_it_matters: Introduces a trajectory-aware, low-latency guardrail with explicit risk modeling, aligning with interests in long-horizon safety for LLM agents and bridging to sequence modeling ideas from time series foundation models.
efficiency.reason: Adaptive allocation across model populations for LLM-driven evolutionary search is relevant for cost-efficient red-teaming/evolutionary program search, but more about budgeting than core security.

efficiency.title: TS-RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation for Time Series Forecasting
efficiency.summary: The paper proposes TS-RAG, a retrieval-augmented approach for time series forecasting that uses specially designed reference tokens to fuse input sequences with retrieved similar sequences. It argues that naive concatenation of references, as in LLM RAG, is ineffective for typical time series models due to limited data, smaller scales, and weaker generative ability. Experiments show TS-RAG achieves consistent state-of-the-art results on several real-world forecasting benchmarks.
efficiency.why_it_matters: It bridges LLM-style RAG with time series by introducing a tailored fusion mechanism, offering a concrete path to leverage retrieval for stronger temporal forecasting without requiring LLM-scale models.
efficiency.reason: Tabular foundation model adaptation via gated skill evolution is relevant for transfer and training-free adaptation methods, but focused on tabular rather than temporal sequence models.

efficiency.title: Runtime Observability for Heterogeneous Attention Memory
efficiency.summary: The paper proposes a runtime observability contract for heterogeneous attention memory that covers four memory classes with three operators, enforces metric-typed composition, and yields an executable request-level risk ledger whose certification tier (formal, partial, empirical) is machine-determined. They instantiate this across six model configurations over five architecture families, validate under 12.4M entry reads with eight-way concurrency and per-request budgets, and maintain zero risk-budget violations while using an always-on fused probe within CUDA graphs. Applied to a served DeepSeek-V4 stack with a packed compressed-KV prototype, the system localizes a silent corruption to a structural boundary and conducts a machine-adjudicated discrimination campaign that rejects two confounded inferences, with all artifacts and Lean proofs released for full regeneration.
efficiency.why_it_matters: It offers a principled, composable, and empirically backed way to quantify and bound memory-related risks in modern LLM serving stacks, directly relevant to secure KV/latent cache compression and recurrent state management in time-series-like attention regimes.
efficiency.reason: Addresses memory/cache observability and runtime contracts across attention/memory mechanisms — relevant for understanding failure modes under compression and for risk accounting in deployed LLMs and agents.

efficiency.title: Learning the Pareto Frontier of Predictive Models under Distribution Shift
efficiency.summary: The paper introduces Frontier Learning, which treats a library of pretrained models with mixed access regimes (black-box predictions and white-box representations) as complementary sources under distribution shift. It builds a unified target-domain feature by concatenating internal representations from white-box models with outputs from black-box models, then trains a lightweight regularized supervised learner, guaranteeing training-sample risk no worse than any single baseline including zero-shot reuse, fine-tuning, or direct training. Experiments on simulations and real-world shifts (DomainNet/VisDA and MIMIC-IV-Notes ICU mortality) show it matches or outperforms the strongest individual reuse strategy, with the largest gains when no single baseline is reliable across the shifts considered.
efficiency.why_it_matters: Provides a simple, access-agnostic ensemble-on-representations approach that subsumes common reuse strategies and is empirically strong under shift—relevant to robustness/security and modular reuse of foundation models.
efficiency.reason: Agentic BO using LLMs to inject priors into optimization touches on agentic systems and leveraging LLMs as components—relevant to attack/defense surfaces and efficient automated red-teaming workflows.

efficiency.title: Taxonomy-Driven Analysis of Open-Source AI Risk Mitigation Tools
efficiency.reason: Using VLMs to encode time-series as images speaks to practical efficiency and cross-modal approaches for time-series analysis and could impact deployment/serving costs for TS workloads.
